newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus says Condor orders six A320s.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says Condor orders six A320s.

text.p: Airbus Industrie said on Thursday that Lufthansa unit Condor Flugdienst signed a contract to buy six A320 single-aisle aircraft.
Condor's A320 will seat 168 passengers in a single-class configuration and will be powered by CFM56 engines from CFM International.
Deliveries of the twin engine jets will begin in the first half of 1998, Airbus said.
Industry sources said the A320 has a market price of about $47 million.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Aerospatiale and Deutsche Airbus have 38 pct each. British Aerospace Plc has 20 pct and CASA of Spain four pct.
Engine maker CFM International is a joint venture between U.S. group General Electric Co and France's SNECMA.
